correctness.rationale: Exact one-variable squared-distance identity and triangular separation density. Ratio h has a unique strict global maximizer: the derivative numerator B has one zero because q'' changes sign once at the root of s cos s - sin s, and B(L²)=0. This rigorously classifies all diametral pairs. Strict Hessian at the interior point yields a square-root tail; first-order endpoint deficit with vanishing separation density yields a quadratic tail. A smooth branch comparison with slope J gives the full pitch-deficit crossover and conditional laws. All boundary, zero-pitch and equal-contact cases are explicit. Included Python 3 code passed 28,036 finite supporting assertions; no finite test is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The object is a canonical finite arc of a constant-curvature, constant-torsion space curve. Its globally farthest pairs undergo a sharp first-order contact switch; the change of the dimension and boundary geometry of maximizers forces a probability exponent jump from 1/2 to 2. The exact critical pitch, nondifferentiable diameter, moving pitch-deficit crossover with a sharp cutoff, and independent conditional endpoint laws make a coherent geometric probability theorem rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
